summary.text: A 25-year-old man presented to the outpatient clinic with a 1-week history of gradually progressive blurred vision and occasional floaters in the left eye, without photophobia, redness or systemic symptoms; the case presentation calls the blurring painless, while the introduction lists pain.
He had no relevant past medical, ocular, surgical or family history, no prior trauma and no features suggestive of systemic autoimmune disease.

Examination showed best-corrected visual acuity 6/6 in the right eye and 6/18 in the left (6/60 with pinhole), intraocular pressure 12 mm Hg bilaterally, and in the left eye fine keratic precipitates, +2 anterior chamber cells, mild vitritis, subretinal exudates, retinal perivasculitis with venous tortuosity and vessel sheathing; OCT showed increased central retinal thickness, foveal contour disruption and subretinal exudates; the Figure 1 caption adds vitreoretinal interface irregularities.

Systemic workup was unremarkable, with negative syphilis, toxoplasma, tuberculosis, ANA, anti-dsDNA and rheumatoid factor results, normal ACE, a complete blood count and ESR without stated abnormality and an unremarkable chest X-ray, leading to a diagnosis of idiopathic ocular vasculitis with anterior uveitis and retinal vasculitis; fluorescein angiography was reported to confirm active vasculitis without described findings.
He received a single posterior sub-Tenon triamcinolone acetonide injection with topical corticosteroids and NSAIDs.

Visual acuity improved from 6/18 to 6/9 with resolution of inflammatory signs; over 6 months of monthly follow-up there was complete resolution, no recurrence or complications, IOP of 10-14 mm Hg and visual acuity maintained at 6/9; contrast sensitivity was not tested; none of the common injection side effects (raised intraocular pressure, cataract progression, scleral perforation) occurred.
